epithet.en: Former Duke of Milan, a powerful sorcerer

2.modern-en: Tells Miranda the story of their exile: his brother Antonio usurped his dukedom twelve years ago with Alonso's help. Reveals he conjured the tempest to bring his enemies to the island. Commands Ariel and confines Caliban.

5.modern-en: Watches unseen as Ferdinand and Miranda fall in love. Approves of the match but pretends to oppose it, testing Ferdinand by making him carry logs.

7.modern-en: Uses Ariel to set a magical banquet before Alonso, Antonio, and Sebastian, then makes it vanish. Through Ariel disguised as a harpy, accuses them of their crimes against him.

8.modern-en: Blesses Ferdinand and Miranda's engagement with a masque of goddesses. Suddenly remembers Caliban's plot and ends the masque. Delivers the 'Our revels now are ended' speech. Sets a trap of glittering clothes to distract the conspirators.

9.modern-en: Renounces his magic, breaks his staff, and drowns his book. Reveals himself to Alonso and forgives his enemies. Reclaims his dukedom. Frees Ariel.

10.modern-en: Delivers the epilogue, asking the audience's applause and indulgence to set him free.

2.modern-en: Watches the shipwreck with pity. Hears her father's story for the first time. Meets Ferdinand and is instantly drawn to him — the first young man she has ever seen besides her father and Caliban.

5.modern-en: Defies her father by offering to carry Ferdinand's logs herself. Confesses her love to Ferdinand and they pledge to marry.

8.modern-en: Watches the masque of goddesses performed for her betrothal.

9.modern-en: Sees Alonso, Antonio, and the others for the first time. Declares 'O brave new world, that has such people in it!' Reunited with civilization.

2.modern-en: Reports on the successful execution of the tempest: the ship is safely hidden, the passengers scattered across the island. Reminds Prospero of the promised freedom. Is told to be patient and sent on further errands.

3.modern-en: Plays invisible music that puts Alonso's party to sleep, foiling Antonio and Sebastian's murder plot by waking Gonzalo just in time.

6.modern-en: Invisible, overhears Caliban plotting with Stephano and Trinculo to murder Prospero. Disrupts their plans by mimicking Trinculo's voice and causing confusion.

7.modern-en: Disguised as a harpy, descends on the magical banquet and delivers Prospero's message of judgment to the three men of sin — Alonso, Antonio, and Sebastian.

8.modern-en: Performs in the masque as the goddess Ceres. Helps set the trap of glittering clothes for Caliban's conspiracy. Drives the plotters away with spirit hounds.

9.modern-en: Brings the ship's crew safely to harbor. Reports that Caliban, Stephano, and Trinculo are captured. Is granted freedom by Prospero at last.

epithet.en: A savage islander, son of the witch Sycorax

2.modern-en: Cursed and enslaved by Prospero after attempting to assault Miranda. Bitterly claims the island was his before Prospero arrived. Is forced to carry wood.

4.modern-en: Encounters Trinculo and Stephano. Mistakes Stephano for a god after tasting wine. Pledges himself as their servant and sings of freedom.

6.modern-en: Persuades Stephano to murder Prospero in his sleep and take Miranda as his wife. Advises them to seize Prospero's books first, as that is the source of his power.

8.modern-en: Tries to keep Stephano and Trinculo focused on the murder plan, but they are distracted by the glittering clothes Prospero has laid as a trap.

9.modern-en: Brought before Prospero in disgrace. Acknowledges his foolishness in worshipping a drunkard and promises to 'seek for grace.'

epithet.en: Son of Alonso, King of Naples

1.modern-en: On the ship during the tempest with his father Alonso and the court.

2.modern-en: Led to Prospero's cell by Ariel's music, grieving his father whom he believes drowned. Meets Miranda and they are immediately enchanted by each other. Prospero tests him by making him a prisoner.

5.modern-en: Willingly carries logs to prove his love for Miranda. They declare their love and pledge to marry, with Prospero's secret approval.

8.modern-en: Watches the masque of goddesses celebrating his betrothal to Miranda.

9.modern-en: Reunited with his father Alonso, who believed him dead. Reveals Miranda as his bride.

1.modern-en: On the ship during the storm. Ordered below deck by the Boatswain.

3.modern-en: Wanders the island grieving for Ferdinand, whom he believes drowned. Is comforted by Gonzalo. Nearly murdered in his sleep by Antonio and Sebastian before Ariel intervenes.

7.modern-en: Confronted by Ariel in harpy form, who accuses him of helping Antonio overthrow Prospero. Stricken with guilt, he wishes himself drowned beside his son.

9.modern-en: Meets Prospero, who he wronged twelve years ago, and begs forgiveness. Discovers Ferdinand alive and playing chess with Miranda. Joyfully blesses their marriage.

epithet.en: Prospero's treacherous brother, current Duke of Milan

1.modern-en: On the ship during the storm. Curses the Boatswain.

3.modern-en: Tempts Sebastian to murder Alonso while he sleeps, proposing that Sebastian would then become King of Naples just as Antonio became Duke of Milan through treachery. They draw swords but are interrupted by Ariel waking Gonzalo.

7.modern-en: Accused by Ariel as one of the three men of sin who wronged Prospero.

9.modern-en: Confronted by Prospero, who calls him unnatural but forgives him and demands his dukedom back. Antonio says nothing — his silence is conspicuous.

1.modern-en: On the ship during the storm.

3.modern-en: Mocks Gonzalo's optimism. Persuaded by Antonio to murder his sleeping brother Alonso and seize the throne of Naples. Interrupted by Ariel.

7.modern-en: Included in Ariel's accusation as one of the three sinners.

9.modern-en: Confronted by Prospero, who knows of his attempted treachery but forgives him.

1.modern-en: Tries to stay cheerful during the storm, joking that the Boatswain looks more likely to hang than drown.

2.modern-en: Revealed as the man who secretly helped Prospero and infant Miranda survive their exile by provisioning their leaky boat with food, water, and Prospero's books.

3.modern-en: Tries to comfort Alonso on the island. Imagines an ideal commonwealth. Falls asleep and is almost killed, but Ariel wakes him just in time.

7.modern-en: Witnesses the magical banquet and Ariel's accusation. Notes that the guilty men are in a trance of despair.

9.modern-en: Thanked and honored by Prospero for his loyalty. Marvels at how the whole ordeal has turned out for the best.

4.modern-en: Stumbles upon Caliban hiding under a cloak. Takes shelter under the same cloak during a storm, creating a comic tableau. Reunites with Stephano.

6.modern-en: Goes along with the plot to murder Prospero, though more focused on drinking. Is confused when the invisible Ariel mimics his voice.

8.modern-en: Distracted by the glittering clothes laid as a trap, ignoring Caliban's warnings to stay focused on the murder.

9.modern-en: Brought before Prospero in disgrace alongside Caliban and Stephano.

4.modern-en: Arrives singing with a bottle of wine, having survived the wreck by floating on a barrel. Gives Caliban wine and is worshipped as a god.

6.modern-en: Agrees to Caliban's plan to murder Prospero and become lord of the island with Miranda as his queen.

8.modern-en: Cannot resist stealing the glittering clothes from Prospero's trap. Chased off by spirit hounds.

9.modern-en: Brought before Prospero. Recognized by Alonso as his missing butler.

1.modern-en: Commands the crew during the tempest. Bluntly tells the noblemen to stay below deck — the waves care nothing for royal titles.

9.modern-en: Brought ashore by Ariel. Reports that the ship is miraculously intact and the crew unharmed.
